title: Youthful Purpose Guru Bill Damon's Golden Opportunity
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart draws on Stanford researcher William Damon's work on youth purpose to offer teachers a single, concrete practice: tell students why you chose teaching, what you find fulfilling about it, and what you hope to accomplish with them. Quoting Damon directly, Stuart clarifies that the point isn't to recruit students into teaching but to model, as an admired adult, what pursuing a vocation with purpose actually looks like. He supplies two worked examples, a longer script recounting his own path from pre-med to teaching, and a shorter, in-the-moment version reacting to something happening in class that day, to show teachers exactly what the practice can sound like. The piece is part of Stuart's larger Rainbow of Why framework for building student Value, with purpose modeling as one specific, practical color on that palette. He closes by encouraging teachers to try the script soon, repeat it often, and enjoy doing it.
points: Citing Damon's research directly, Stuart identifies a single, low-cost teacher practice, narrating your own vocational purpose, as a golden opportunity for building student purpose.
He supplies two fully worked scripts, long and short, rather than only describing the idea abstractly, making the practice immediately usable.
The practice is explicitly framed as modeling, not recruitment: the goal is showing what purposeful adulthood looks like, not persuading students to become teachers.
This piece situates purpose-modeling as one specific color within Stuart's broader Rainbow of Why framework for cultivating student Value.
quotes: There's this researcher out of Stanford who basically dedicated his life to studying why some people enter adulthood with a strong sense of purpose and others don't.

One golden opportunity to [give young people purposeful role models] is for teachers to tell students why they chose teaching as a profession, what they find fulfilling about teaching and what they hope to accomplish with their students.
The point of doing this is not to persuade their students to become teachers but rather to show what it looks like for an admired adult to pursue a vocation with purpose.
It was a very striking moment for me because I didn't really like much what I had seen the doctor doing, and I wasn't really interested in medicine like I thought that I would be.

So it was a few months later when I went to a Boys and Girls Club in Chicago, and I got to work with all these young people there at the Club, and I just suddenly realized, 'Wow, this is really cool; I really like to work with young people.'
And finally, have FUN doing it. Because it IS fun to get to be a purpose exemplar for young people.
